main_text.l: te animis, ne perfidè agatis. Malach. 2.

l.i: Congrediar autè vobiscum judicio, e-roq;
celer testis in præstigiatores, in adul-
teros, in perjuros, in eos quì mercede frau-
dant mercenarios, qui viduas, qui pu-
pillos, qui peregrinos labefactant, neque
me timent, inquit armipotens Iova.
Tu ergo, nate[?], corpus tuum ab omni
fœditate & impudicitia tuere, L. neve
committito ut omissa uxore tua flagi-
tium admittas: H. & uxorem ducito de
cognatione tua, non ullius generis, quod
à majorum tuorum stirpe sit alienum.
Nos enim de vatum progenie sumus.
Memoria repete, fili, Abrahamum, Isa-
cum,

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the mark after "cavete" and after "nate" is a printed sign (a curved stroke, possibly a tilde or abbreviation) that I could not identify, so both are marked [?]. "e-roq;" is uncertain and marked [?]. The final word is broken across the line as "Isa-" / "cum," and is given with the printed hyphen. Long s is plain s throughout. The "L." and "H." before "neve" and "uxorem" are printed inline section letters, kept in the text.
